subject: health
title: Correction and reflection: deciding what to keep, drop, and add each season
focus: deciding what to keep, drop, and add each season
essentialQuestion: What has to keep happening when no one reminds me?
keyPoints: Seasonal review asks what still serves the purpose, what creates burden, what condition changed, and which single addition or removal is feasible.
A durable plan names the goal, constraints, feasible options, support and backup routes, plus the evidence or condition that should trigger review and revision.

For deciding what to keep, drop, and add each season, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Build an independent maintenance system with a normal-week version, a hard-week fallback version, and a written restart procedure. Progress is described in terms of behaviors kept, never body measurements.
studentTask: Build a decision organizer for a fictional person working on deciding what to keep, drop, and add each season. Record the goal, two influences or constraints, two options, the safest feasible choice, a support or backup route, and the evidence that would trigger a later revision.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in deciding what to keep, drop, and add each season; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the deciding what to keep, drop, and add each season task using the supplied fictional or public case.
The response uses at least two accurate details from the lesson instruction and distinguishes evidence from assumption.
The response gives a safe, feasible next step or support route and does not depend on private disclosure, body comparison, or recorded media proof.
adaptationChoices: The system may be written, tabled, built as a checklist, entered in a calendar, or described aloud to an adult. Any component the learner cannot perform is planned as a supported or adapted component and scored equally.
extensionChallenge: Apply deciding what to keep, drop, and add each season under a new constraint, compare two approaches, or explain the idea to someone else with an original fictional example, without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
